rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. The child reproduces C18's distinctive two-paragraph explanation of why tax-refund limitation periods remain applicable after a judicial or administrative reinterpretation, including nearly identical language about finality, lost records, burdens of proof and administration, and discrimination against similarly situated taxpayers. It also follows the same operative sequence: describe untimely refund claims, acknowledge that part of the claim was already barred when the law changed, note that a timely filing opportunity nevertheless existed for another portion, defend the limitations policy, and reject individualized relief. C10 and C05 share substantial language and machinery, but C18 is materially closer and more extensive.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Congress has determined it to be a sound policy to include in the revenue system a statute of limitations which, after a period of time, bars taxpayers from obtaining refunds of tax overpayments and bars the Government from collecting additional taxes. Such a provision is essential to finality in tax administration.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Congress has determined it to be sound policy to include in the revenue system a statute of limitations which, after a period of time, bars taxpayers from obtaining refunds of tax overpayments and bars the Government from collecting additional taxes. Such a provision is essential to finality in tax administration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The basic justification for the statute of limitations is that, after the passing of a reasonable period of time, witnesses may have died, records may have been destroyed or lost, and problems of proof and administration of tax claims become too burdensome and unfair for both taxpayers and the Government.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The basic justification for a statute of limitations is that, after the passing of a reasonable period of time, witnesses may have died, records may have been destroyed or lost, and problems of proof and administration of tax claims become too burdensome and unfair for both taxpayers and the Government.
shared_material.explanation: Essentially verbatim articulation of the evidentiary and administrative rationale.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The basic purposes underlying the statute of limitations continue in force even in cases where a taxpayer, after having paid a tax, discovers that the interpretation of the law has been changed by a judicial decision or by a modification in regulations and rulings.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The basic purposes underlying the statute of limitations continue in force even in cases where, after payment of a tax, the interpretation of the law is changed by a judicial decision or by a modification in regulations and rulings.
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim language tailored only slightly to the child's judicial-decision facts.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is true that, at the time the District Court reversed the Internal Revenue Service's interpretation of the statute, refund of taxes paid for a large portion of the period here involved was barred by the statute of limitations. However...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: While it is true that, at the time the second ruling of the Internal Revenue Service was published, refund for the year 1949 already was barred by the statute of limitations, the taxpayers did have...in which to file a timely claim for 1950.
shared_material.explanation: Parallel factual framing: acknowledge that the change in interpretation came too late for part of the refund period, then emphasize that the claimants still had time to preserve another part.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There are no special circumstances in this case to justify singling out the named taxpayers for special relief from the statute of limitations. The bill, therefore, would unfairly discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This bill, by singling out two of these taxpayers for special relief from the statute of limitations, would unjustly discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated.
shared_material.explanation: The same concluding application of the limitations policy to reject special relief as discriminatory.
